picker.title: Which instrument do you play?
picker.subtitle: Chords, scales and theory are shown for the instrument you pick. You can switch any time.
picker.guitar: Chord shapes on the neck, scale positions, progressions, song analysis and more.
picker.piano: Chords and scales on the keyboard: inversions, two-hand voicings and fingerings.

home.title: Don't memorise chords — understand how they're built
home.subtitle: Every chord's formula, notes, fretboard position and sound on one page. From open chords to thirteenths.

chords.title: Chords
chords.description: Open, barre, sus, 7th, 9th, 11th and 13th chords: formula, notes and fingering.

scales.title: Scales
scales.description: Major, minor, pentatonic, blues and the modes across the whole neck.

fretboard.title: Chord finder
fretboard.description: Pick notes on the fretboard and see which chord you're playing.

progressions.title: Progressions
progressions.description: Pick a key and see its notes, chords and common progressions. Swap any chord for an alternative.

builder.title: Chord builder
builder.description: Add degrees one by one and see and hear how the chord changes.

song.title: Song helper
song.description: Type the chords: find the key, transpose it and pick a capo spot.

intervals.title: Intervals
intervals.description: See third, fifth and octave shapes from any note on the neck.

circle.title: Circle of fifths
circle.description: A map of all 12 keys: key signatures and neighbouring chords.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.description: Every term in plain words, with sound examples.

how.title: How is a chord built?
how.body: A chord is built by stacking [[third|thirds]] on a [[root|root]]. 1 – 3 – 5 is a [[triad|triad]]. Add the 7th [[degree|degree]] and you get a [[seventhChord|seventh chord]], then come the 9th, 11th and 13th. Every chord page shows its formula and where it sits on the neck.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Your choices are saved in this browser.
settings.accentHint: Colour of buttons, root notes and selected items.
settings.leftHandedHint: Mirrors the fretboard and chord diagrams.
settings.tuningHint: Tuning applies to the fretboard. Chord diagrams are for standard tuning.

tunings.standard: Standard (E A D G B E)
tunings.dropD: Drop D (D A D G B E)
tunings.openG: Open G (D G D G B D)

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.description: The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has moved.

credits.details: guitar — University of Iowa, piano — VSCO 2

practice.question: Question {{current}} of {{total}}
practice.noWeakest: No weak spots yet. Keep going.

keys.title: Key puzzles
keys.description: Find the key from its chords, pick the chord that does not belong, or fill the gap in a progression.
keys.promptKey: Which key are these chords in?
keys.manyKeys: These chords fit more than one key; any of them counts.
keys.startHint: The chords will play; press any chord to hear it on its own.

ear.title: Note by ear
ear.description: The lit note plays first, then a second one. Find the second note by ear and press it on the instrument. Each question starts somewhere new on the neck or keys.
ear.prompt: Which note came after the lit one?
ear.startHint: Browsers only start sound after a click: press the button to begin.

find.title: Find the note
find.description: Find the note on the instrument, or name the spot that is lit.
find.promptName: Which note is the lit spot?

circle.title: Circle of fifths drill
circle.description: Count steps round the circle, find keys by their signature and their relatives. Answer on the circle.
circle.signatureNone: Which major key has no sharps or flats?
circle.relativeToMinor: What is the relative minor of {{from}} major?
circle.relativeToMajor: What is the relative major of {{from}} minor?
circle.startHint: Each question can be a different kind.

intervals.title: Interval drill
intervals.description: Hear the gap between two notes and name it, or build an interval from a given note on the instrument.
intervals.promptEar: What is the interval between these two notes?
intervals.startHintEar: Two notes will play; pick the interval from the buttons below.
intervals.startHintBuild: A note will light up on the instrument; press the asked interval at its exact pitch.
intervals.needTwo: Pick at least 2 intervals for by-ear practice.

play.guitarHint: Tap anywhere on the neck and play freely.
play.pianoHint: Tap the keys and play freely. On a computer keyboard, A W S E D F T G Y H U J K play too.
